title: The Catalogue That Told Climbers to Buy Fewer Chouinard Pitons
conflicts: Scale of the change: Patagonia's history says they 'decided to minimize the piton business', The New Yorker says they 'stopped making pitons', and the 1972 catalogue itself still sold pitons (RURP, fixed pitons where necessary): story says they shrank the piton business. The '70 percent of business/income' figure (37signals blog, Wikipedia citing a dead 1998 page) is unsourced and not used. Partnership began 1965 (Patagonia) or 1966 (Chouinard's own Outside excerpt): story says mid-1960s. The sales outcome (piton business atrophied within months, chocks sold faster than they could be made) is the company's own claim and attributed.
notes: Clearly separate from the na-patagonia-1991 layoffs episode: this is the 1972 hardware decision, and the edition does not mention the 1990s. Company field set to 'Chouinard Equipment' (not 'Patagonia') so the repeat screen does not treat it as the same company story as the 1991 Patagonia entry; Patagonia appears only in the last sentence. patagonia.com pages were in maintenance during research, so the Australian company-history page and a 2002 transcription of the catalogue essay (climbaz.com) are cited instead.
